key_insight: SOLE-R1 uses a video-language reasoning model that self-observes egocentric robot video to provide the sole reward signal for on-robot RL, yielding robust task learning under partial observability and distribution shift.
problem_solved: Current vision-language evaluators used as rewards in RL are brittle: under partial observability and domain shift they produce perceptual errors that policies exploit instead of solving tasks. SOLE-R1 addresses this by grounding reward in temporal video-language reasoning tailored to on-robot data.
method: Train/deploy a video-language reasoning model (Self-Observing LEarner) that scores behavior by analyzing egocentric video relative to language task prompts.
Use the VLM's video-grounded score as the sole reward signal for on-robot reinforcement learning, closing the loop between perception and control.
Improve robustness via temporal reasoning and on-robot adaptation/calibration so rewards reflect true task success rather than transient perceptual artifacts.
impact: Provides a scalable way to supervise on-robot RL with language-based rewards that generalize better under real-world partial observability and distribution shift, reducing reliance on hand-designed rewards or extensive human labeling.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: egocentric video + language instruction → SOLE-R1 video-language reasoner → reward signal → on-robot RL loop
Before vs After comparison: policy exploiting VLM errors (failure) vs policy trained with SOLE-R1 (robust success) shown as side-by-side task outcomes
Temporal attention / multi-frame visualization showing how the model uses video context to avoid single-frame perceptual mistakes
Performance chart: success rate under distribution shift / partial observability comparing baseline evaluators and SOLE-R1
paper_title: SOLE-R1: Video-Language Reasoning as the Sole Reward for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Philip Schroeder, Thomas Weng, Karl Schmeckpeper, Eric Rosen, Stephen Hart
